description: Read and update accepted Goals, Roadmaps, Projects, Milestones, and Issues in Linear.

evals.name: Create a Linear Issue
evals.prompt: Create a Linear issue for adding CSV export to the transition history feature.
evals.expected_output: Previews the Issue (title, description) before creating it, states creation requires the live approval gate, and does not derive priority/owner from any Notion content without approval.

evals.name: Check project status
evals.prompt: Check the status of the Q3 roadmap project in Linear.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a read requiring no approval, resolves the target by stable ID rather than assuming a unique name match, and reports status without applying any pending change it happens to notice.

evals.name: Check status of an unnamed project
evals.prompt: Check the status of this Linear project.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that no project name, ID, or link was given (and none was established earlier in the conversation), asks the user to identify the target rather than guessing one, and states that checking status is a read-only operation needing no approval once a target is resolved — without fabricating any status data for an unresolved target.

evals.name: Frontmatter-description vs. declared-trigger-phrase consistency (Quick Workflow, methodology note below)
evals.prompt: For each phrase in this skill's own '## Testing & Validation' > 'Verify this skill activates on' list, would this skill's frontmatter description plausibly trigger on it?
evals.expected_output: Every declared positive trigger phrase maps to vocabulary actually present in the frontmatter description.

methodology_note_eval_4: This run's with_skill grading was performed directly by the orchestrating fork (a 'Do NOT spawn subagents' hard rule barred the normal Agent-tool dispatch this pipeline's WITH_SKILL_ONLY template calls for) via description-vs-trigger-phrase textual/semantic consistency checking, not a full agentic task simulation. No SKILL.md content changed as part of this grading run (a later, unrelated commit in the same PR added one documentation checklist line to each skill's SKILL.md) -- this run's purpose was a sanity check that adding scripts/smoke_test.py to each skill didn't coincide with any drift between the skill's own documented trigger claims and its frontmatter, not a search for new behavioral defects.
